headlines.text: Flash back to 2022, when the ROH World Heavyweight Title made its debut as Jonathan Gresham vs. Dalton Castle battled for the honor of being first champion, appearing on Battle of the Belts, rated 6.56. The very first Ring of Honor World Championship match to air on AEW programming ? a respectful, tightly-worked title defense that ended in Gresham's signature Octopus submission.
Rewind to 2020, when AEW welcomed Lance Archer for the first time against Colt Cabana, appearing on Dynamite, rated 5.45.

Back on this day in 2026, Willow Nightingale vs. Kamille fought tooth and nail for the AEW TBS Title, appearing on Dynamite, rated 3.83. For Kamille, it marked a first real shot at championship gold. It was the 70th time the AEW TBS Title had been on the line, a genuinely rare milestone for that title. Every title match carries a little extra weight, and this one was no exception.

secondaries.text: It was 2022 when it was title-change night for the AEW TNT Title as Sammy Guevara vs. Scorpio Sky battled it out, appearing on Battle of the Belts, rated 5.41 ? ending the champion's reign at 2 defenses. A shocking heel turn ? Guevara stooped to a low blow to steal the title back from Sky, in front of a hometown Texas crowd that had been fully behind the returning champion.
That Friday in 2022, the AEW World Heavyweight Title was up for grabs as Adam Page vs. Adam Cole went to war in a Texas Death Match, appearing on Rampage, rated 7.82 ? a good, competitive contest.
Turning the clock back to 2020: Suge D made their AEW debut against Sammy Guevara, appearing on Dynamite, rated 4.00.
